title: 2012 AMC 10A Problem 22
statement: The sum of the first \(m\) positive odd integers is \(212\) more than the sum of the first \(n\) positive even integers. What is the sum of all possible values of \(n?\)

solutions.text:
The first \(m\) positive odd integers sum to \(m^2\), and the first \(n\) positive even integers sum to \(n(n+1)\). Thus \(m^2=n(n+1)+212\).

As a quadratic in \(n\), this has discriminant \(1-4(212-m^2)=4m^2-847\), which must be an odd square. Let \(p^2=4m^2-847\). Then \((2m+p)(2m-p)=847\).

The positive factor pairs of \(847\) are \(847\cdot1\), \(121\cdot7\), and \(77\cdot11\). They give \(p=423,57,33\), respectively.

Because \(n=\dfrac{-1+p}{2}\), the possible values of \(n\) are \(211,28,16\). Their sum is \(255\).

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Use that the first \(m\) odd numbers sum to \(m^2\)
